title: Establishment of an Inter-Ministerial Standing Committee under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
decision_details: - The United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) was established in 1982 as a result of the declaration of a Charter on the Rights of Women by the United Nations General Assembly and adoption of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women in 1979. Sri Lanka has ratified the said Convention and is responsible for following constitutional procedures, enacting legislation and providing periodic reports as required. Based on the recommendations made by the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women in relation to Sri Lanka under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, the Ministry in charge of the subject of Women's Affairs, in collaboration with the Ministry in charge of the subject of Foreign Affairs and other relevant ministries/institutions, prepares a periodic report once in every 04 years. Accordingly, the Ninth (09) Periodic Report prepared by Sri Lanka has been submitted to the 90th Session of the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women held in Geneva, Switzerland from 3rd to 21st February 2025. It has been identified the necessity of having an integrated approach regarding mandatory reporting and follow-up obligations, at a review held under the Chairmanship of the Hon. Prime Minister and with the participation of other parties, regarding the concluding observations on the Periodic Report made during that Session.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Women and Child Affairs to establish an Inter-Ministerial Standing Committee, enabling to pursue action accordingly and to enter into relevant policy decisions, was approved by the Cabinet.
